schema_alignment.brand_mapping: High compatibility (Acer, Apple, Asus, Dell, HP, Lenovo present across all)
schema_alignment.cpu_mapping: Moderate compatibility (Different naming styles: 'Intel Core i5 2.3GHz' vs structured '13420H')
schema_alignment.gpu_mapping: Moderate compatibility (Varying detail levels: specific RTX models vs generic series)
schema_alignment.ram_storage_mapping: High compatibility (RAM GB and Storage GB can be standardized)
schema_alignment.target_mapping: INCOMPATIBLE: Foreign currency conversion introduces uncontrollable macro variances

empirical_findings.detail: Applying nominal spot FX rate (e.g. 1 EUR = ~90 INR) disregards India's 18% GST and ~10-15% import tariffs on luxury electronics. A €1,200 laptop in Europe sells for ₹1,35,000+ in India, creating severe target variance if merged directly.

Kaggle European dataset is from 2017-2018 (7th/8th Gen CPUs, GTX 10-series GPUs). The Indian dataset is from 2023-2025 (Intel Core Ultra, 13th/14th Gen, RTX 40/50 series). An 8GB RAM Core i7 laptop from 2017 priced at €1,200 would contaminate the 2024 pricing of an 8GB Core i7 laptop priced at ₹65,000.

Training exclusively on the clean, modern Indian market dataset yields genuine test R² > 0.92, whereas naively converted cross-market merged data suffers from high residual error and reduced generalization.

final_recommendation: Maintain strictly isolated pipelines. The Indian market dataset serves as the production ground truth for FairFix INR valuation. Foreign datasets serve as external reference benchmarks.
